Omnidirectional Connectivity From Random Dipoles

Source: R/dp-omni.R
dp_omni.Rd

Usage

dp_omni(
  resistance,
  radius,
  source_strength = NULL,
  destination = NULL,
  source_threshold = 0.01,
  radius_units = c("pixels", "km"),
  resistance_is = "resistances",
  normalize = TRUE,
  n_draws = 32,
  n_dipoles = 1e+05,
  seed = NULL,
  power = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

resistance

A terra::SpatRaster or file path: the resistance (or conductance) surface. Or a circuit from dp_circuit(), to reuse its factorization.

radius

Numeric. The dispersal radius: pairs of cells are counted if their centres are at most this far apart. In pixels by default (see radius_units). Inf counts all pairs.

source_strength

Optional terra::SpatRaster or file path on the same grid: source strength, e.g. habitat suitability. If NULL (default), the conductance surface is used, as in os_run(). With a destination, this is the origin strength.

destination

Optional terra::SpatRaster or file path on the same grid: destination strength, e.g. habitat suitability in another period or season. If given, only pairs of an origin and a destination cell count. Default NULL: pairs of cells of one surface.

source_threshold

Numeric. Cells with source (or destination) strength below this are not sources (or destinations). Default 0.01.

radius_units

Character. "pixels" (default): the radius counts cells, so the kernel is the cells with \(dr^2 + dc^2 \le\) radius\(^2\), as in os_run(). "km": great-circle distance between cell centres on lon/lat grids (the kernel narrows in degrees of longitude towards the poles), or distance in the coordinate reference system's units, converted to km, on projected grids.

resistance_is

Character. Whether resistance holds "resistances" (default) or "conductances". Ignored for a circuit.

normalize

Logical. Also compute flow potential and normalized current. Default TRUE.

n_draws

Integer. Number of draws (solves). Default 32.

n_dipoles

Integer. Number of dipoles per draw. Default 1e5.

seed

Integer or NULL. Seed for the random draws. If NULL (default), one is drawn from R's random number generator, so set.seed() also makes runs reproducible. The seed used is returned as the "seed" attribute.

power

Logical. Also map the power dissipated (see "Power" in dp_omni()), and with normalize, normalized power. Default FALSE.

progress

Logical. Report progress through the 'progressr' package (see "Progress" in dp_omni()). Default TRUE; it shows only when a 'progressr' handler is active.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster with layers current; with normalize, flow_potential and normalized_current; with power, power; and with both, normalized_power. Attributes: "halves", a data frame comparing the estimates from odd and even draws on source (and destination) cells (Spearman's \(\rho\) and the median relative difference), for current and the normalized and power layers; and "seed".

Details

Maps omnidirectional connectivity among habitat, in the role of os_run(), with the random-dipole method: many random source-sink pairs superposed on one factored circuit, which takes about n_draws solves whatever the number of pairs.

With a destination, it maps connectivity between two distributions instead: the routes linking origin cells (source_strength) to destination cells within radius, for example present to future habitat, breeding to wintering grounds, or foraging to roosting habitat. The map is undirected: every pair counts whichever way it flows, so swapping the two surfaces gives the same map. For the net flow from one to the other, with its direction, see dp_flux().

Current flows along the circuit's links: the resistors joining each cell to its 8 neighbours (see dp_circuit()). For each link \(e\), the method estimates $$T_e = \sum_{i \ne j} w_i w_j k(d_{ij}) I_e(i,j)^2$$ over ordered pairs of cells, where \(w\) is source strength, \(k\) is 1 for cells within radius of each other and 0 otherwise, and \(I_e(i,j)\) is the current through \(e\) when one unit flows from \(i\) to \(j\) on the whole circuit. A cell's current combines the links that meet at it, up to 8: \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}\sum_{e \ni \mathrm{cell}} T_e}\), where the half is because each link is shared by the two cells it joins. For a unit flow, a link's squared current is the derivative of the pair's effective resistance with respect to that link's resistance, so the map is the sensitivity of habitat-weighted pairwise resistance to degrading each cell.

With a destination, the pair weights are \(o_i d_j k(d_{ij})\), with \(o\) the origin (source_strength) and \(d\) the destination strength. Since \(I_e(i,j)^2 = I_e(j,i)^2\), only the unordered pairs matter, and the map is the same whichever surface is the origin. A cell's pair with itself carries no current. Cells in both distributions take part at both ends, unlike in dp_flux(), where their flow cancels. With one surface, \(o = d = w\).

With two surfaces, the pairs have a mean dipole, whose current (the directional map of dp_flux()) is solved exactly. Each draw's dipoles are centered on it, so the draws estimate only the variance of the pairs' currents, and the mean's exact squared current is added back. The estimate is still unbiased, but where the pairs' currents mostly agree in direction its noise is much smaller: by a factor of about \(1 - R\), with \(R\) as in dp_directionality(). With one surface, the mean dipole is zero.

Each draw injects n_dipoles unit dipoles, pairs drawn in proportion to \(w_i w_j k(d_{ij})\), each with a random sign, and solves the circuit once. The random signs make the cross terms between dipoles average out, so the mean squared current over draws, scaled by \(S / M\) (\(S\) the sum of pair weights, \(M\) = n_dipoles), estimates \(T_e\) without bias. Values don't depend on n_dipoles, and runs with different settings are comparable.

Pairs never span groups of cells that are separated by NA cells, since no current can pass between them. Cells with source strength below source_threshold, or NA, are not sources.

Flow potential is the same estimate on the uniform circuit (conductance 1 on the same cells) with the same dipoles, and normalized current is current divided by flow potential: above 1 where current is channelled, below 1 where it is impeded. Unlike os_run(), flow potential uses the same circuit shape as current, not a square box per target.

The result differs from os_run()'s by design: squared rather than absolute current, and the whole circuit rather than a window around each target. Current maps typically agree closely (Spearman's \(\rho \approx\) 0.95–0.99), normalized current less so (\(\rho \approx\) 0.85). No current is added at endpoints for the injected current itself, unlike Circuitscape's cell maps.

Power

With power = TRUE, the result also maps the power dissipated, which picks out choke points: places where current is forced through resistance. A link's power is its squared current (summed over pairs, as for current) times its resistance, \(1 / g_e\). A cell's power is half the sum over its links, so each link's power is shared between the two cells it joins, and the cells sum to the circuit's total. It comes from the same per-link sums as current, so it costs no extra solves, and its estimate is unbiased with about twice the relative noise of current.

This is not current squared times the cell's resistance. A link's resistance depends on both cells it joins (with Circuitscape's averaged conductances, it approaches twice the lower of the two resistances where they differ widely), and diagonal links' resistance is \(\sqrt{2}\) times larger. Squaring a current map and multiplying by resistance overstates power on high-resistance cells next to low-resistance ones, where choke points often are.

With normalize, normalized_power is power divided by the power of the same pairs on the uniform circuit. Unlike normalized current, it has the units of resistance (the uniform circuit's links have resistance 1), so compare it within a surface rather than across surfaces in different units.

Accuracy

Each draw contributes noise with a relative standard deviation of about 1.4, so per-cell noise falls as \(1/\sqrt{\mathrm{n\_draws}}\): in tests at the default 32 draws, about 6–12% in current and 3–10% in normalized current. More dipoles per draw help only until pairs are well covered (about \(10^5\)). The "halves" attribute compares estimates from the odd and even draws, an estimate of the noise of a run.

Reproducibility

Results are determined by seed, the settings and the circuit: each draw has its own random stream, so they don't depend on the number of Julia threads (beyond the last bits of rounding, which can depend on the linear algebra library's threading). Random streams can change between Julia versions.

Performance

The time is mostly the factorization (one, or two with normalize) and the solves; it barely depends on radius. Draws are sampled and link currents summed in parallel over Julia's threads; set the number with cs_setup(). To reuse factorizations across runs, pass a circuit from dp_circuit().

Progress

The dipole functions report progress through the 'progressr' package: one step per factorization and, for each batch of draws, one for sampling its dipoles and one per circuit solved (current, and with normalize, flow potential), plus one per solve of the mean flow with a destination. Draws are solved in batches of 8 to 32 (fewer on larger grids), so at the default 32 draws most runs are one batch. Nothing is shown unless a handler is active, e.g. progressr::with_progress(dp_omni(...)) or, in a 'shiny' app, progressr::withProgressShiny(dp_omni(...)); see progressr::handlers(). Reporting doesn't change the results. Set progress = FALSE to signal nothing at all.

See also

dp_circuit(), dp_pairwise(), dp_flux(), os_run()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # circuitscaper::cs_julia_available(circuitscape = FALSE)
resistance <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/resistance.tif",
                                      package = "circuitscaper"))
result <- dp_omni(resistance, radius = 15, seed = 1)
terra::plot(result)
attr(result, "halves")

# Connectivity between two distributions
origin <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/source.tif", package = "circuitscaper"))
destination <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/ground.tif", package = "circuitscaper"))
between <- dp_omni(resistance, radius = 45, source_strength = origin,
                   destination = destination, seed = 1)
terra::plot(between)
DONTSHOW({JuliaConnectoR::stopJulia()})
}
